entities.summary: Antonio Millo (158 chars): Antonio Millo, active during 1557–1590, was a captain and cartographer who authored isolarios and portolan charts and atlases. He explored the Mediterranean and Atlantic, mapping the coastlines of North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula. His charts were used by navigators and traders, facilitating maritime commerce and navigation. The precise and detailed maps he created set a new standard for nautical charting, influencing cartography for centuries to come. The accuracy of his maps was so renowned that they were used by subsequent cartographers, including Ortelius and Mercator. Millo's work also reflects the growing importance of maritime trade during the Renaissance, as European powers sought to expand their economic influence. His legacy can be seen in the continued use of portolan charts and the development of modern navigation techniques. The precision of his maps has allowed for more efficient and safe navigation, saving countless lives and vessels. The impact of Millo's work can be felt in the modern era, where accurate cartography remains crucial for global trade and commerce.
